## Introduction & Data Source

This analysis evaluates morphological variations among Antarctic penguin species observed at the Palmer Station.

The dataset used in this analysis is from the R package `palmerpenguins`, created by Allison Horst, Alison Hill, and Kristen Gorman. Learn more on the [palmerpenguins official site](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/).

---

## 1. Data Cleaning and Preparation

We load the `palmerpenguins` package alongside `tidyverse` to filter out missing records and inspect key variables.

```{r}
#| label: r-data-prep
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Clean dataset removing NA values in body metrics
penguins_clean <- penguins %>%
  drop_na(species, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, sex) %>%
  mutate(
    species = as.character(species),
    bill_ratio = bill_length_mm / bill_depth_mm
  )

glimpse(penguins_clean)

#| label: r-summary-table
bill_summary <- penguins_clean %>%
  group_by(species, island) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bill_len = mean(bill_length_mm),
    mean_bill_dep = mean(bill_depth_mm),
    mean_bill_ratio = mean(bill_ratio),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_bill_ratio))

knitr::kable(bill_summary, digits = 2, col.names = c("Species", "Island", "Count", "Mean Length (mm)", "Mean Depth (mm)", "Bill Length/Depth Ratio"))

#| label: fig-r-bill-dimensions
#| fig-cap: "Bill Length vs. Bill Depth across Palmer Penguin Species."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5

ggplot(penguins_clean, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, color = species, shape = sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Bill Morphological Dimensions by Species",
    subtitle = "Exhibiting Simpson's Paradox across overall vs. species-level trends",
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Bill Depth (mm)",
    color = "Species",
    shape = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

Summary of Results
Simpson's Paradox in Action: If we looked at the dataset as a whole without grouping by species, bill depth and length would appear uncorrelated or negatively correlated. However, within each individual species, there is a clear positive correlation between bill length and bill depth.

Species Cluster Distinctiveness:

Adélie: Short bill length, high bill depth.

Chinstrap: Long bill length, high bill depth.

Gentoo: Long bill length, low bill depth.
